title_en: A page of advice: the long sentence
q_en: How do I read a long sentence, and follow the thread of the argument from line to line?
q_ar: كَيْفَ أَقْرَأُ جُمْلَةً طَوِيلَةً، وَكَيْفَ أَتَّبِعُ خَيْطَ الْكَلَامِ مِنْ سَطْرٍ إِلَى سَطْرٍ؟
not_yet: Every word of a classical page: you read the frame and the thread first, and gloss the rare words.
Why the writer chooses one word of a pair and not another: it is his style, not a rule to work out.
Reading the page without the vowels: from Lesson 80.
not_yet_ar: كُلُّ كَلِمَةٍ فِي صَفْحَةٍ قَدِيمَةٍ: نَقْرَأُ الْإِطَارَ وَالْخَيْطَ أَوَّلًا وَنَسْأَلُ عَنِ الْكَلِمَاتِ النَّادِرَةِ.
لِمَاذَا يَخْتَارُ الْكَاتِبُ كَلِمَةً مِنَ الزَّوْجِ دُونَ أُخْرَى: هَذَا أُسْلُوبُهُ، لَا قَاعِدَةٌ تُسْتَنْتَجُ.
قِرَاءَةُ الصَّفْحَةِ بِلَا حَرَكَاتٍ: مِنَ الدَّرْسِ ٨٠.

sents: مَا مِنْ طَالِبٍ إِلَّا وَلَهُ مُعَلِّمٌ.
There is no student who has not a teacher.
مَا مِنْ بَيْتٍ إِلَّا وَفِيهِ كِتَابٌ.
There is no house without a book in it.
مَا مِنْ خَيْرٍ إِلَّا وَالتَّقْوَى طَرِيقٌ إِلَيْهِ.
There is no good but taqwā is a way to it.
مَا مِنْ شَرٍّ إِلَّا وَالتَّقْوَى حِفْظٌ مِنْهُ.
There is no evil but taqwā is a protection from it.

lines: Cover what follows إِلَّا. What is left?
Which little word is between مَا and the noun? Its ending?
أَيُّ حَرْفٍ بَيْنَ «مَا» وَالِاسْمِ؟ وَمَا حَرَكَتُهُ؟
Is what follows إِلَّا a new sentence? What does it say?
هَلْ مَا بَعْدَ «إِلَّا» جُمْلَةٌ جَدِيدَةٌ؟ مَاذَا تَقُولُ؟

slides.head_en: A long sentence is made of short pieces

cards.def_ar: نَنْفِي الْجِنْسَ كُلَّهُ ثُمَّ نَقُولُ: إِلَّا هَذَا.
cards.def_en: Deny the whole kind, then name what is always there.
Two opposites cover everything between them.
“And of that”: one more item of the list.
Wonder at how much there is.

rows: soon and later: this life and the next
outward and inward: what is seen and what is in the heart
slides.note: The two words of a pair take the same ending: they follow the noun they describe.
slides.note_ar: تَتْبَعُ الْكَلِمَتَانِ الِاسْمَ الَّذِي قَبْلَهُمَا فِي حَرَكَتِهِ.

slides.head_en: The same frame: about good, about evil
slides.head_ar: الْإِطَارُ نَفْسُهُ: فِي الْخَيْرِ وَفِي الشَّرِّ
rows: taqwā is a way to it
taqwā is a protection from it
slides.note: The little word after the noun answers the question: إِلَيْهِ = to it; مِنْهُ = from it.
slides.note_ar: الْحَرْفُ بَعْدَ الِاسْمِ يُجِيبُ: «إِلَيْهِ» = الطَّرِيقُ إِلَى الْخَيْرِ، وَ«مِنْهُ» = الْحِفْظُ مِنَ الشَّرِّ.

slides.head_en: Cutting the long sentence into its pieces
rows: taqwā is a road that reaches it
and a means that carries to it
slides.note: The answer has two parts joined by وَ, both ending in ـٌ.
slides.note_ar: لِلْجَوَابِ قِسْمَانِ بَيْنَهُمَا وَاوٌ، وَكِلَاهُمَا يَنْتَهِي بِالضَّمَّةِ.

slides.head_en: One sentence, cut at its commas
lines: فَمَا مِنْ خَيْرٍ عَاجِلٍ وَلَا آجِلٍ ظَاهِرٍ وَلَا بَاطِنٍ،
There is no good, present or future, outward or inward,
but taqwā is a road that reaches it,
and a means that carries to it.
slides.source: al-Naṣāʾiḥ al-Dīniyya wa-l-Waṣāyā al-Īmāniyya of Imām ʿAbdallāh b. ʿAlawī al-Ḥaddād (chapter on taqwā)

slides.head_en: Look: the thread of a list
sents: Of that: happiness in this world.
And of that: knowledge and understanding.
And of that: Paradise in the Hereafter.

items: مَا مِنْ طَالِبٍ إِلَّا وَلَهُ مُعَلِّمٌ
there is no student who has not a teacher
in this world and the next
how many students the Habib has advised!
مَا مِنْ شَرٍّ إِلَّا وَالتَّقْوَى حِفْظٌ مِنْهُ
there is no evil but taqwā is protection from it
taqwā is the road of happiness

slides.wrong: مَا مِنْ خَيْرٌ إِلَّا وَالتَّقْوَى طَرِيقٌ إِلَيْهِ
slides.why: Wrong ending! After مِنْ the noun ends in kasra (here tanwīn kasra): مَا مِنْ خَيْرٍ.
slides.why_ar: خَطَأٌ فِي الْحَرَكَةِ! بَعْدَ «مِنْ» يَكُونُ الِاسْمُ مَجْرُورًا: مَا مِنْ خَيْرٍ.

slides.head_en: The thread of the page: a list, line after line
slides.head_ar: خَيْطُ الصَّفْحَةِ: قَائِمَةٌ سَطْرًا بَعْدَ سَطْرٍ
lines: وَكَمْ عَلَّقَ اللهُ الْعَظِيمُ فِي كِتَابِهِ الْعَزِيزِ عَلَى التَّقْوَى مِنْ خَيْرَاتٍ عَظِيمَةٍ
How many great goods the Mighty God has attached to taqwā in His noble Book!
فَمِنْ ذَلِكَ الْمَعِيَّةُ الْإِلَهِيَّةُ الْحِفْظِيَّةُ اللُّطْفِيَّةُ
Of that: the divine companionship of protection and gentleness.
And of that: knowledge direct from God.
slides.source: al-Naṣāʾiḥ al-Dīniyya wa-l-Waṣāyā al-Īmāniyya of Imām ʿAbdallāh b. ʿAlawī al-Ḥaddād (chapter on taqwā)

can: I can find the frame مَا مِنْ … إِلَّا … in a long sentence, and say what it denies and what it states.
I can read pairs of opposites (عَاجِلٌ وَآجِلٌ، ظَاهِرٌ وَبَاطِنٌ) and say what they cover together.
I can follow a list through a page by the words وَمِنْ ذَلِكَ, and read كَمْ + a past verb as “how many!”.
can_ar: أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَجِدَ الْإِطَارَ «مَا مِنْ … إِلَّا …» وَأَقُولَ مَا يَنْفِي وَمَا يُثْبِتُ.
أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَقْرَأَ أَزْوَاجَ الْمَعَانِي (عَاجِلٌ وَآجِلٌ، ظَاهِرٌ وَبَاطِنٌ) وَأَقُولَ مَا تَشْمَلُ.
أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَتْبَعَ الْقَائِمَةَ بِ«وَمِنْ ذَلِكَ» وَأَقْرَأَ «كَمْ» مَعَ الْفِعْلِ الْمَاضِي تَعَجُّبًا.

sections.name: A
sections.en: Four lines from the same page of advice. Read it aloud, then answer.
lines: وَمَا مِنْ شَرٍّ عَاجِلٍ وَلَا آجِلٍ، ظَاهِرٍ وَلَا بَاطِنٍ إِلَّا وَالتَّقْوَى حِرْزٌ حَرِيزٌ، وَحِصْنٌ حَصِينٌ لِلسَّلَامَةِ مِنْهُ، وَالنَّجَاةِ مِنْ ضَرَرِهِ
And there is no evil, present or future, outward or inward, but taqwā is a sure safeguard and a strong fortress for safety from it and escape from its harm.
وَمِنْ ذَلِكَ الْفُرْقَانُ عِنْدَ الِاشْتِبَاهِ وَوُقُوعِ الْإِشْكَالِ، وَالْكَفَّارَةُ لِلسَّيِّئَاتِ، وَالْمَغْفِرَةُ لِلذُّنُوبِ
And of that: discernment at times of confusion and difficulty, the wiping out of bad deeds and the forgiveness of sins.
And of that: the promise of Paradise.
وَمِنْ ذَلِكَ الْكَرَامَةُ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ
And of that: honour in this world and the next.
sections.source: al-Naṣāʾiḥ al-Dīniyya wa-l-Waṣāyā al-Īmāniyya of Imām ʿAbdallāh b. ʿAlawī al-Ḥaddād (chapter on taqwā)
sections.cite: ʿAbdallāh b. ʿAlawī al-Ḥaddād, al-Naṣāʾiḥ al-Dīniyya wa-l-Waṣāyā al-Īmāniyya, Shamela Master Library copy (Bafaqih 22222 install, id 184250, 409 pp; no publisher or year on the digital copy), pages 28–29 of the copy (its own pagination); printed edition not identified. The SSD also has PDFs of 102, 432 and 468 pp (one with takhrīj) which were not read. The page has eight lines: line 1 is on slide 7, lines 3-5 on slide 11, and lines 2, 6, 7 and 8 are Exercise A. The Qurʾān verses that follow each «وَمِنْ ذَلِكَ» in the source are left out (abridged). Vowels added by the course (vowelled for learners).
sections.teacher_note: The two ★ rows are for adults and older students; children may skip them. Help the class with the glossed words; the aim is the frame and the thread, not every word.

items.ar_q: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ (الْجُمْلَةَ الطَّوِيلَةَ).
items.model: And there is no evil, present or future, outward or inward, but taqwā is a sure safeguard and a strong fortress for safety from it and escape from its harm.

items.ar_q: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
items.model: And of that: discernment at times of confusion and difficulty, the wiping out of bad deeds and the forgiveness of sins.

items.ar_q: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَيْنِ الثَّالِثَ وَالرَّابِعَ.
items.model: And of that: the promise of Paradise. And of that: honour in this world and the next.

items.en: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
items.ar_q: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
items.model: A page of counsel (advice) with long sentences, from al-Naṣāʾiḥ al-Dīniyya of Imam ʿAbdallāh b. ʿAlawī al-Ḥaddād, the chapter on taqwā.

items.en: Which two words make the frame of line 1?
items.ar_q: أَيُّ كَلِمَتَيْنِ تَصْنَعَانِ إِطَارَ السَّطْرِ الْأَوَّلِ؟
options: مَا مِنْ … إِلَّا: “there is no … but …”.
A sure safeguard, and a strong fortress.
items.answer: مَا مِنْ … إِلَّا: “there is no … but …”.
items.model: مَا مِنْ … إِلَّا: “there is no … but …”.

items.ar: عَاجِلٍ وَلَا آجِلٍ، ظَاهِرٍ وَلَا بَاطِنٍ
items.en: Line 1 has two pairs of opposites. What do they mean?
items.ar_q: فِي السَّطْرِ الْأَوَّلِ زَوْجَانِ مِنَ الْأَضْدَادِ. مَا مَعْنَاهُمَا؟
items.model: Present or future (this life or the next); outward or inward.

items.en: Line 1 gives two pictures of what taqwā is for the evil. Name them.
items.ar_q: فِي السَّطْرِ الْأَوَّلِ صُورَتَانِ لِلتَّقْوَى. اُذْكُرْهُمَا.
options: A sure safeguard, and a strong fortress.
مَا مِنْ … إِلَّا: “there is no … but …”.
items.answer: A sure safeguard, and a strong fortress.
items.model: A sure safeguard, and a strong fortress.

items.en: What two things does the fortress give? Find the two nouns.
items.ar_q: مَا الشَّيْئَانِ اللَّذَانِ يُعْطِيهِمَا الْحِصْنُ؟ جِدِ الِاسْمَيْنِ.
items.model: Safety (السَّلَامَةُ) from it, and escape (النَّجَاةُ) from its harm.

items.en: Line 2 lists three things. Which word joins the last two?
items.ar_q: فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّانِي ثَلَاثَةُ أَشْيَاءَ. أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَجْمَعُ الْأَخِيرَيْنِ؟
items.model: وَ. The three things are discernment, the wiping out of bad deeds, and the forgiveness of sins; وَ comes before the second (وَالْكَفَّارَةُ) and before the third (وَالْمَغْفِرَةُ).

items.en: Lines 2, 3 and 4 each begin with the same words. Which, and what do they tell the reader?
items.ar_q: تَبْدَأُ السُّطُورُ ٢ وَ٣ وَ٤ بِالْكَلِمَاتِ نَفْسِهَا. مَا هِيَ؟ وَمَاذَا تَقُولُ لِلْقَارِئِ؟
items.model: وَمِنْ ذَلِكَ: “and of that”. Each line is one more item of the list of what taqwā brings.

items.ar_q: جِدِ الْكَلِمَةَ الَّتِي تَعْنِي «Paradise».
options: مَا مِنْ … إِلَّا: “there is no … but …”.
A sure safeguard, and a strong fortress.
items.model: الْجَنَّةِ.

items.en: True or false: line 4 speaks only about the Hereafter.
items.ar_q: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ: يَتَكَلَّمُ السَّطْرُ الرَّابِعُ عَنِ الْآخِرَةِ فَقَطْ.
items.model: False. “In this world and the next”: honour in both.
items.note: “In this world and the next”: honour in both.

items.en: Read the vowels of line 1. What ending does each of these three words have, and why?
items.ar_q: اِقْرَأِ الْحَرَكَاتِ فِي السَّطْرِ الْأَوَّلِ. مَا حَرَكَةُ آخِرِ كُلِّ كَلِمَةٍ مِنْ هَذِهِ الثَّلَاثِ؟ وَلِمَاذَا؟
items.model: شَرٍّ: ـٍ (after مِنْ). حِرْزٌ: ـٌ (what taqwā is: the statement). السَّلَامَةِ: ـِ (after لِـ).

items.en: ★ Line 1 says taqwā protects from every evil, and lines 2–4 say what good it brings. Why would the writer put both on one page?
items.ar_q: ★ فِي السَّطْرِ الْأَوَّلِ التَّقْوَى حِفْظٌ مِنَ الشَّرِّ، وَفِي الْبَاقِي هِيَ طَرِيقُ الْخَيْرِ. لِمَاذَا جَمَعَ الْكَاتِبُ بَيْنَهُمَا؟
items.model: Taqwā works in two directions: it keeps harm away and it brings good. Putting them together shows that one thing does both.

items.en: ★ Line 1 says “present or future”, and line 4 says “in this world and the next”. What is the same, and what does it do for the page?
items.ar_q: ★ فِي السَّطْرِ الْأَوَّلِ «عَاجِلٌ وَآجِلٌ» وَفِي الرَّابِعِ «الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةُ». مَا الَّذِي يَتَشَابَهُ؟ وَمَاذَا يَفْعَلُ بِالصَّفْحَةِ؟
items.model: The same pair of worlds, said in two ways. The page ends where it began: with both worlds.

sections.name: B
sections.en: A short text: how to read a long passage. Read it aloud, then answer.
lines: جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَ عُمَرَ فِي مَجْلِسِ الْحَبِيبِ بَعْدَ الصَّلَاةِ.
Ahmad sat with Umar in the Habib’s majlis after the prayer.
فَتَحَ الْحَبِيبُ الْكِتَابَ وَقَرَأَ كَلَامًا طَوِيلًا.
The Habib opened the book and read a long passage.
فَسَأَلَ عُمَرُ: يَا حَبِيبُ، الْكَلَامُ طَوِيلٌ، فَكَيْفَ أَفْهَمُهُ؟
Umar asked: Habib, the passage is long, so how do I understand it?
قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: مَا مِنْ كَلَامٍ طَوِيلٍ إِلَّا وَفِيهِ مَعْنًى وَاحِدٌ.
The Habib said: There is no long passage but there is one meaning in it.
اِبْدَأْ بِالْكَلِمَاتِ الصَّغِيرَةِ، فَهِيَ مِفْتَاحُ الْكَلَامِ.
Begin with the little words, for they are the key of the speech.
ثُمَّ اُنْظُرْ إِلَى «وَمِنْ ذَلِكَ»: بَعْدَ هَذِهِ الْكَلِمَاتِ يَأْتِي شَيْءٌ جَدِيدٌ.
Then look at “and of that”: after these words something new comes.
فَقَرَأَ عُمَرُ الْكَلَامَ مَرَّةً أُخْرَى وَقَالَ: الْآنَ فَهِمْتُ، يَا حَبِيبُ!
So Umar read the passage once more and said: Now I understand, Habib!
قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: وَاجْلِسْ بِأَدَبٍ ظَاهِرًا وَبَاطِنًا.
The Habib said: And sit with good manners, outwardly and inwardly.
وَكَتَبَ أَحْمَدُ فِي كِتَابِهِ: الصَّبْرُ مِفْتَاحُ الْفَهْمِ، وَالْفَهْمُ سَعَادَةٌ.
And Ahmad wrote in his book: Patience is the key of understanding, and understanding is happiness.
وَرَجَعَ أَحْمَدُ وَعُمَرُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ سَعِيدَيْنِ.
And Ahmad and Umar went back to the house, happy.
sections.teacher_note: The two ★ rows are for adults and older students; children may skip them.

items.en: Where did Ahmad sit, and with whom? (line 1)
items.ar_q: أَيْنَ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ؟ وَمَعَ مَنْ؟
options: In the Habib’s majlis, with Umar.
A long passage from the book.
That something new is coming: the next item of the list.
items.answer: In the Habib’s majlis, with Umar.
items.model: In the Habib’s majlis, with Umar.

items.ar_q: مَاذَا قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ؟
options: A long passage from the book.
With the little words, for they are the key of the speech.
He read the passage once more and said: Now I understand.
items.answer: A long passage from the book.
items.model: A long passage from the book.

items.en: Who asks this question, and what is his problem?
items.ar_q: مَنْ يَسْأَلُ هَذَا السُّؤَالَ؟ وَمَا مُشْكِلَتُهُ؟
items.model: Umar. The passage is long, and he does not know how to understand it.

items.ar_q: تَرْجِمِ السَّطْرَ الرَّابِعَ.
items.model: The Habib said: There is no long passage but there is one meaning in it.

items.en: ★ Umar first says the passage is long, then says “Now I understand”. What did the Habib change: the passage, or the way of reading it?

items.model: The way of reading it: he showed him where to look first (the little words, the frame, the thread). The passage stayed as long as before.

items.en: ★ The Habib says “sit with good manners, outwardly and inwardly”. How is this advice about reading, and not only about sitting?
items.ar_q: ★ يَقُولُ الْحَبِيبُ: «اِجْلِسْ بِأَدَبٍ ظَاهِرًا وَبَاطِنًا». كَيْفَ هُوَ نَصِيحَةٌ فِي الْقِرَاءَةِ وَلَيْسَ فِي الْجُلُوسِ فَقَطْ؟

sections.en: What kind of text is this, and how do you know? Choose from: a Qurʾān with commentary, a ḥadīth with its chain, a short ethical ḥadīth, a fiqh ruling, a creed, counsel, a long page of advice.

items.ar: يُسَنُّ رَفْعُ الْيَدَيْنِ فِي أَرْبَعَةِ مَوَاضِعَ.
items.en: What kind of text is this, and how do you know?
items.ar_q: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَكَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
items.model: A fiqh ruling: the ruling verb يُسَنُّ (“it is recommended”) names the ruling.

items.ar: مَنْ دَلَّ عَلَى خَيْرٍ فَلَهُ مِثْلُ أَجْرِ فَاعِلِهِ.
items.en: What kind of text is this, and how do you know?
items.ar_q: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَكَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
items.model: A short ethical ḥadīth: مَنْ … فَلَهُ = a condition and its reward.

items.ar: حَدَّثَنِي أَحْمَدُ عَنْ عُمَرَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ
items.en: What kind of text is this, and how do you know?
items.ar_q: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَكَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
items.model: The start of a ḥadīth with its chain of narrators: حَدَّثَنِي … عَنْ … عَنْ ….

items.en: What kind of text is this, and how do you know?
items.ar_q: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَكَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
items.model: Counsel: the commands عَلَيْكَ بِـ (hold to) and إِيَّاكَ وَ (beware of).

items.ar: اللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ بَصِيرٌ، وَالْقُدْرَةُ لَهُ وَاجِبَةٌ.
items.en: What kind of text is this, and how do you know?
items.ar_q: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَكَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
items.model: A creed: it names attributes (صِفَات) of God and says which are obligatory (وَاجِب).

items.ar: قَوْلُهُ: (التَّقْوَى) أَيْ خَوْفُ اللَّهِ وَحِفْظُ النَّفْسِ.
items.en: What kind of text is this, and how do you know?
items.ar_q: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَكَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
items.model: A commentary: قَوْلُهُ names the words commented on, and أَيْ gives their meaning.

items.ar: مَا مِنْ خَيْرٍ إِلَّا وَالتَّقْوَى طَرِيقٌ إِلَيْهِ، وَمِنْ ذَلِكَ السَّعَادَةُ.
items.en: What kind of text is this, and how do you know?
items.ar_q: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَكَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
items.model: A page of advice with long sentences: the frame مَا مِنْ … إِلَّا and the thread وَمِنْ ذَلِكَ.

sections.name: L
sections.en: Translate into English.

items.ar: مَا مِنْ طَالِبٍ فِي تَرِيمَ إِلَّا وَلَهُ مُعَلِّمٌ.
items.model: There is no student in Tarim who has not a teacher.

items.ar: وَمِنْ ذَلِكَ السَّعَادَةُ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ.
items.model: And of that: happiness in this world and the next.
Hold to taqwā, outwardly and inwardly.

items.ar: مَا مِنْ خَوْفٍ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَلَا فِي الْآخِرَةِ إِلَّا وَالتَّقْوَى أَمَانٌ مِنْهُ.
items.model: There is no fear, in this world or the next, but taqwā is safety from it.

items.ar: وَكَمْ سَمِعَ أَحْمَدُ مِنْ دَرْسٍ فِي مَجْلِسِ الْحَبِيبِ!
items.model: How many lessons Ahmad has heard in the Habib’s majlis!

items.ar: السَّعَادَةُ الْعَاجِلَةُ فِي الدُّنْيَا، وَالسَّعَادَةُ الْآجِلَةُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ.
items.model: The near happiness is in this world, and the later happiness in the Hereafter.

items.ar: مَا مِنْ كَلَامٍ طَوِيلٍ إِلَّا وَفِيهِ مَعْنًى وَاحِدٌ، فَاقْرَأْهُ بِصَبْرٍ.
items.model: There is no long passage but it has one meaning: so read it with patience.

items.ar: مَا مِنْ طَرِيقٍ إِلَى الْخَيْرِ إِلَّا وَفِيهِ صَبْرٌ، وَمِنْ ذَلِكَ الصَّبْرُ عَلَى الدَّرْسِ.
items.model: There is no road to good without patience in it; and of that: patience with the lesson.

items.ar: قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: التَّقْوَى بَابُ كُلِّ خَيْرٍ. وَمِنْ ذَلِكَ الْعِلْمُ، وَمِنْ ذَلِكَ الْعَمَلُ. وَمَا مِنْ طَالِبٍ يَخَافُ اللَّهَ إِلَّا وَهُوَ سَعِيدٌ.
items.model: The Habib said: Taqwā is the door of every good. And of that: knowledge, and of that: action. And there is no student who fears God but he is happy.

sections.name: N
sections.en: Find the mistake.

items.ar: مَا مِنْ طَالِبٌ إِلَّا وَلَهُ مُعَلِّمٌ.
items.en: What is wrong with the ending of طَالِبٌ?
items.ar_q: مَا الْخَطَأُ؟
items.model: After مِنْ the noun ends in kasra: مَا مِنْ طَالِبٍ.

items.ar: مَا مِنْ بَيْتٍ إِلَّا وَفِيهِ كِتَابًا.
items.en: What is wrong with the ending of the last word?
items.ar_q: مَا الْخَطَأُ؟
items.model: The thing that is in the house is the one that is there: it ends in ـٌ: وَفِيهِ كِتَابٌ. (ـًا would be an object.)

items.ar: مَا مِنْ خَيْرٍ إِلَّا وَالتَّقْوَى طَرِيقٌ إِلَيْهِ.
items.en: A student translates: “There is some good that taqwā does not reach.” What is wrong?
items.ar_q: مَا الْخَطَأُ؟
items.model: مَا مِنْ … إِلَّا denies the whole kind: there is no good at all without taqwā being a way to it. The student read the denial as “some”.

It is said that the Imam was born in Tarim.
It was said to the boy: Knowledge is light.
عَلَّمَ الْحَبِيبُ الْوَلَدَ: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ وَسَلِّمْ عَلَى سَيِّدِنَا مُحَمَّدٍ ﷺ.
The Habib taught the boy: O Allah, bless and grant peace to our master Muḥammad ﷺ.
The boy reminded his friend of the prayer.
فِي اللَّيْلِ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْأَصْحَابِ وَقَرَأَ الرَّاتِبَ.
At night the boy sat with the companions and read the Rātib.
قَالُوا: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ.
They said: Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, and Allah is greater.
فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ مَعَ أَبِيهِ.
On the Night of Qadr the boy sat in the mosque with his father.
The boy helped the guests and honoured them.
The students helped one another in the ribāṭ.
The boy was humble and learned from them.
اِنْتَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ الْحَبِيبَ عِنْدَ بَابِ الْمَسْجِدِ.
The boy waited for the Habib at the door of the mosque.
اِجْتَمَعَ الطُّلَّابُ فِي الصَّبَاحِ وَاسْتَمَعَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْحَبِيبِ.
The students gathered in the morning and the boy listened to the Habib.
حَجَّ أَبُو الْوَلَدِ ثُمَّ رَجَعَ مِنْ مَكَّةَ.
The boy’s father made the pilgrimage, then returned from Mecca.
أَخَذَ الْوَلَدُ التَّمْرَ مِنْ أَبِيهِ وَقَدَّمَهُ لِلضُّيُوفِ.
The boy took the dates from his father and offered them to the guests.
The boy heard a ḥadīth with its chain.
قَالَ الرَّاوِي: حَدَّثَنَا وَأَخْبَرَنَا، ثُمَّ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: إِنَّمَا الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ.
The narrator said: He told us, and he informed us, then the Prophet ﷺ said: Deeds are only by intentions.
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: قُلْ آمَنْتُ بِاللَّهِ فَاسْتَقِمْ.
The boy heard from the Habib: The Prophet ﷺ said: Say: I believe in Allah, and then be upright.
The boy stood up and said: I believe in Allah.
مَشَى الْوَلَدُ مَعَ أَبِيهِ إِلَى الزِّيَارَةِ وَوَصَلَ فِي الْمَسَاءِ.
The boy walked with his father to the ziyāra and arrived in the evening.
The boy made duʿāʾ: O Allah, guide us.
جَاءَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْمَجْلِسِ وَقَالَ: مَا أَحْسَنَ هَذَا الْمَجْلِسَ!
The boy came to the majlis and said: How beautiful this majlis is!
قَالَ لِأُمِّهِ: جِئْتُ إِلَى الْمَجْلِسِ وَرَأَيْتُ الْحَبِيبَ.
He said to his mother: I came to the majlis and I saw the Habib.
كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ كَلِمَاتٍ مِنْ جَذْرٍ وَاحِدٍ: عَلَّمَ، مُعَلِّمٌ، تَعْلِيمٌ.
The boy wrote words from one root: ʿallama, muʿallim, taʿlīm.
And he wrote: sāfara, musāfir, safar.
نَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى مِنْبَرِ الْمَسْجِدِ وَمِحْرَابِهِ.
The boy looked at the minbar of the mosque and its miḥrāb.
قَالَ الْوَلَدُ: أَنَا حَضْرَمِيٌّ مِنْ تَرِيمَ.
The boy said: I am a Ḥaḍramī, from Tarim.
نَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ بِنَفْسِهِ فِي الْمُعْجَمِ وَوَجَدَ مَعْنَى الْكَلِمَةِ.
The boy looked in the dictionary by himself and found the meaning of the word.
ثُمَّ كَتَبَ الْجَذْرَ وَالْمَعْنَى فِي كِتَابِهِ.
Then he wrote the root and the meaning in his book.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ مَتْنًا صَغِيرًا.
The boy read a small matn (a short base text) with the Habib.
أَصْبَحَ الْمَتْنُ سَهْلًا لَكِنَّ الدَّرْسَ طَوِيلٌ.
The matn became easy, but the lesson is long.
جَاءَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الدَّرْسِ مُسْرِعًا وَجَلَسَ مُسْتَقْبِلَ الْقِبْلَةِ.
The boy came to the lesson hurrying, and sat facing the qibla.
And the Habib was pleased with him.
ذَكَرَ الْوَلَدُ اللَّهَ كَثِيرًا وَصَلَّى عَلَى النَّبِيِّ ﷺ ثَلَاثًا.
The boy remembered Allah a great deal and prayed for blessings on the Prophet ﷺ three times.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ الدَّرْسَ مَرَّتَيْنِ طَلَبًا لِلْعِلْمِ.
The boy read the lesson twice, seeking knowledge.
The Habib gave the boy a small book.
ظَنَّ الْوَلَدُ الْكِتَابَ صَعْبًا فَقَالَ: لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ.
The boy thought the book difficult, so he said: There is no power and no strength except through Allah.
كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ أَرْكَانَ الْوُضُوءِ: الْأَوَّلُ النِّيَّةُ، وَالثَّانِي غَسْلُ الْوَجْهِ.
The boy wrote the pillars of the ablution: the first, the intention; and the second, washing the face.
وَالثَّالِثُ غَسْلُ الْيَدَيْنِ، وَالرَّابِعُ مَسْحُ بَعْضِ الرَّأْسِ.
And the third, washing the hands; and the fourth, wiping part of the head.
The boy read the wird in the morning.
ثُمَّ دَعَا: يَا رَبِّ، اِهْدِنَا وَاعْفُ عَنَّا، آمِينَ.
Then he made duʿāʾ: O my Lord, guide us and pardon us. Amen.
شَرِبَ الْوَلَدُ مِنْ مَاءِ الْمَسْجِدِ وَمَا شَرِبَ إِلَّا مَاءً طَاهِرًا.
The boy drank from the water of the mosque, and he drank only pure water.
Neither its colour nor its taste had changed.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ اِسْمَ الشَّيْخِ عَلَى الْكِتَابِ: سَالِمُ بْنُ يُوسُفَ.
The boy read the shaykh’s name on the book: Salim son of Yusuf.
And his kunya is Abū Aḥmad.
رَغِبَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْعِلْمِ وَالْأَجْرِ وَرَغِبَ عَنِ الْإِثْمِ.
The boy desired knowledge and reward, and turned away from sin.
فَقَالَ لَهُ الْحَبِيبُ: لَا تَرْغَبْ فِي الدُّنْيَا.
So the Habib said to him: Do not set your desire on this world.
اِسْتَيْقَظَ الْوَلَدُ قَبْلَ الْفَجْرِ وَأَخَذَ السِّوَاكَ.
The boy woke up before dawn and took the siwāk.
Then he sat and strove in his wird.
The boy never missed the rawḥa.
يَحْضُرُ الْوَلَدُ الرَّوْحَةَ دَائِمًا وَهُوَ سَعِيدٌ جِدًّا.
The boy always attends the rawḥa, and he is very happy.
A letter arrived from the boy’s uncle.
بَدَأَ الْعَمُّ رِسَالَتَهُ: أَمَّا بَعْدُ، فَاطْلُبِ الْعِلْمَ.
The uncle began his letter: Now then, seek knowledge.
قَالَ الْوَلَدُ لِأُمِّهِ: هَذَا هُوَ الْكِتَابُ الَّذِي قَرَأْتُهُ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ.
The boy said to his mother: This is the book that I read with the Habib.
It is a small book that I read three times.
ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ لِيَحْضُرَ الدَّرْسَ.
The boy went to the mosque to attend the lesson.
قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: لِيَتَعَلَّمْ كُلُّ طَالِبٍ كَيْ يَعْمَلَ بِعِلْمِهِ.
The Habib said: Let every student learn, so that he may act on his knowledge.
The Habib said: Whoever serves, learns.
وَإِذَا جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ فَهِمَ الدَّرْسَ.
And when the boy sat in the majlis, he understood the lesson.
كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ: وُلِدَ الْإِمَامُ فِي صَفَرَ سَنَةَ أَلْفٍ وَأَرْبَعٍ وَأَرْبَعِينَ.
The boy wrote: The Imam was born in Ṣafar, in the year one thousand and forty-four.
قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ آيَةً ثُمَّ قَرَأَ تَفْسِيرَهَا.
The Habib read a verse, then read its commentary.
ثُمَّ قَالَ: الْحِكْمَةُ، أَيِ الْعِلْمُ وَالْعَمَلُ.
Then he said: Wisdom, that is, knowledge and action.
قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ الْإِسْنَادَ ثُمَّ الْمَتْنَ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: الدِّينُ النَّصِيحَةُ.
The Habib read the chain, then the matn: The Prophet ﷺ said: Religion is sincere counsel.
وَقَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: مَعْنَى الْحَدِيثِ: عِمَادُ الدِّينِ النَّصِيحَةُ.
And the Habib said: The meaning of the ḥadīth: the pillar of religion is sincere counsel.
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: مَنْ دَلَّ عَلَى خَيْرٍ فَلَهُ مِثْلُ أَجْرِ فَاعِلِهِ.
The boy heard in the majlis: The Prophet ﷺ said: Whoever guides to good has a reward like that of the one who does it.
ثُمَّ دَلَّ الْوَلَدُ صَدِيقَهُ عَلَى الْمَجْلِسِ.
Then the boy guided his friend to the majlis.
قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ فِي الرَّوْحَةِ مِنَ الْمَتْنِ: يُسَنُّ رَفْعُ الْيَدَيْنِ فِي أَرْبَعَةِ مَوَاضِعَ.
In the rawḥa the Habib read from the matn: Raising the hands is recommended in four places.
ثُمَّ سَأَلَ الْحَبِيبُ: مَا حُكْمُ رَفْعِ الْيَدَيْنِ؟ فَقَالَ الْوَلَدُ: سُنَّةٌ.
Then the Habib asked: What is the ruling on raising the hands? The boy said: A sunna.
قَرَأَتْ مَرْيَمُ عَقِيدَةً صَغِيرَةً فِي الْبَيْتِ وَسَمِعَهَا الْوَلَدُ.
Maryam read a small creed at home, and the boy listened to her.
She said: Allah exists; He is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.
قَالَ أَبُو الْوَلَدِ: يَا بُنَيَّ، عَلَيْكَ بِأَدَاءِ الْأَمَانَةِ وَإِيَّاكَ وَالْخِيَانَةَ فِيهَا.
The boy’s father said: My son, hold fast to returning what is entrusted, and beware of betraying it.
And hold fast to truthful speech and to keeping a promise.
قَرَأَ الْحَبِيبُ نَصِيحَةً طَوِيلَةً عَنِ التَّقْوَى.
The Habib read a long counsel about taqwā (God-consciousness).
وَمَعْنَاهَا: مَا مِنْ خَيْرٍ عَاجِلٍ وَلَا آجِلٍ إِلَّا وَالتَّقْوَى سَبِيلٌ إِلَيْهِ.
And its meaning: There is no good, present or future, but taqwā is a road to it.
